punchline: Women who first answered a few phone questions were more than twice as likely to let strangers search their cupboards for two hours.
thirty_sec: In California, housewives were phoned and asked a few questions about household products. Three days later, they were asked to let five or six men come in for two hours and go through their cupboards. Of those who had answered the questions, 52.8 percent agreed, against less than half as many among those asked only the big request. Yes! by Goldstein, Martin and Cialdini draws the point: a small yes prepares a larger one.
